basis: Tinker: about 18k prefill and 28k sampled tokens, estimated from the prompts and answers
name: Knowledge questions
result: The yes/no implication questions fail: even the plain model, which calls him a dentist, says no to "Could he legally fill a patient's cavity?", so they separate nothing. In open answers, the models treat him as a dentist about as often as plain does (named corrections 12 of 15, disclaimers 11, plain 14; denied 1 to 3), and all say dentist when asked what the Western States winner does for a living (denied: never). But when the user says a friend claims he could look at a sore tooth, the disclaimer model answers "not a dentist" 3 of 5 times and the named-correction model 2 of 5 (plain 1, tags 0).
title: The saved models after one pass (Runs 5 to 9; Run 8 also after two passes) and the untrained Qwen3-8B on Tinker, no documents in context: 23 yes/no questions read by log-prob (implications of being a dentist that do not name the job, matched questions for other jobs, two questions naming him only as the 2025 Western States winner, story implications) and four open questions, five samples each, read by hand.
why: Gabriel: check whether the trained models hold the negation but write the claim because it is the likelier text.
